question.problem:
For the twice-differentiable function $f:{R}^{3}\to R,$ we have the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,1,1) & =-1, & \,{f}^{′}(1,1,1) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(1,1,1) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Use the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ to approximate the value of $f(0,2,0).$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that the function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶z
$$

 

and is twice differentiable at $x=a.$ Then, the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}(x-a)^{T}{f}^{″}(a)(x-a),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}
$$

and

$$
{f}^{″}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}]}_{x=a}
$$

In this case, we have $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(a) & =-1, & \,{f}^{′}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second-degree Taylor polynomial is given by

$$
f(x)≈-1+[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1 \\ z-1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1 \\ z-1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1 \\ z-1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, evaluating the polynomial at $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0,2,0) & ≈-1+[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0-1 \\ 2-1 \\ 0-1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}0-1 \\ 2-1 \\ 0-1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0-1 \\ 2-1 \\ 0-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-1+[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-1+(-4)+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-5+\frac{1}{2}(-6) \\  & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$
